week_in_brief: The ground shifted for regional grocers: full ad automation became mandatory, private label crossed 95%, and a state banned AI pricing—all in the same week.

items.headline: Platform AI Now Runs Your Campaigns
items.whats_happening: Google Ads updated its Terms of Service on July 1, making AI-driven creative generation and campaign optimization the default setting. Advertisers can no longer disable automation—Google's systems now control creative, bidding, and budget allocation. TikTok launched its Agentic Hub marketplace for AI campaign management; Meta revealed a complete AI advertising system at Cannes. The shift is industry-wide: marketing platforms are moving to autonomous operation.
items.so_what: You must audit what these systems are doing with your budget, especially across multiple locations. Build first-party data (email, purchase history, loyalty behavior) aggressively—it's the only lever you control when platforms automate everything else.

items.headline: Private Label Outpaces National Brands for First Time
items.whats_happening: Daymon's Q2 report shows 95% of US consumers now buy private label, with 69% purchasing on most or every trip. Private label unit sales outpassed national brands for the first time. AWG added 64 new private label items in Q2 alone. The shift isn't about discounting anymore—it's about quality, values, and trust. Shoppers view private label as a primary choice, not a fallback.
items.so_what: Your owned brand is your marketing moat. Invest in quality, packaging, and storytelling that reflects your community identity. National chains can't replicate your local credibility—lean into that. Recalibrate CPG partnerships around co-marketing your private label, not just theirs.

items.headline: New Jersey Bans AI Surveillance Pricing; ESL Pause
items.whats_happening: New Jersey passed the first state law banning AI-driven dynamic pricing and placing a moratorium on electronic shelf labels in grocery stores. The law prohibits using surveillance data to charge different prices for the same product at the same store. Expect other states to follow—this is consumer backlash meeting regulatory momentum.
items.so_what: If you operate in or near New Jersey, clarify your pricing transparency now. Even if you're not using dynamic pricing, shoppers are suspicious—name your pricing strategy publicly and tie it to fairness and consistency. That messaging matters more than the technology you're not using.

items.headline: GLP-1 and Platform Control Push First-Party Capture
items.whats_happening: GLP-1 users now reduce grocery spending by 2.7% annually, with heavy cuts in impulse and snacking categories but growth in protein and wellness. At the same time, platforms (Google, Meta, TikTok) automated campaign execution and eliminated opt-outs. SMS earns $0.74 per send versus $0.15 for generic campaigns—a 5x difference driven by behavioral triggers and owned audience data. Zero-click searches now account for 68% of Google queries; visibility depends on earned media and citations, not just paid ads.
items.so_what: Capture shopper data at checkout and through loyalty. Use SMS for time-sensitive offers tied to behavior, not segments. Adjust category mix toward protein, prepared wellness, and functional beverages—and make sure your marketing reflects those shifts. Earned media (PR, community participation, expert content) now rivals paid for visibility in AI-driven search.

this_weeks_take: Regional grocers face a new operating reality: platforms control the campaigns, private label is the primary brand, and shoppers distrust surveillance. Your advantage is what the nationals can't automate—local trust, community positioning, and first-party relationships built in-store. Own that or lose it.
